author: Lucan Velvetquill, playwright (banned in two holds)
pages:
#Dramatis Personae

^Hilde, a blacksmith of great strength and greater shyness
^Arvid, a travelling bard of small talent and large hat
^Old Marta, the innkeeper, who has seen everything twice
^A goat

#Scene the First: The Forge

^(HILDE hammers at a horseshoe. ARVID enters, strumming.)

ARVID: Fair smith! Your hammer rings like the bells of the high temple!

HILDE: It is a hammer. It rings like a hammer.

ARVID: And your arms! Like two mighty oaks!

HILDE: (blushing furiously) I have work to do.

ARVID: Then I shall compose a ballad while you work. Ahem. Oh, maiden of the anvil, oh, lady of the coals...

^(HILDE drops the horseshoe on her own foot. The goat wanders in and eats ARVID's sheet music.)

#Scene the Second: The Inn

^(Evening. OLD MARTA polishes a tankard.)

MARTA: You've been mooning at that bard for a week, girl.

HILDE: I have not been mooning. I have been... observing his technique.

MARTA: His technique is terrible. He rhymed "anvil" with "anvil". Twice.

HILDE: He is very brave to perform with such little skill.

MARTA: (aside, to the audience) Ah. She's done for.

^(ARVID enters, hat askew, chased by the goat.)

#Scene the Third: The Proposal

^(Night. The forge. ARVID kneels holding a wobbly iron ring.)

ARVID: I made this myself. In your forge. While you slept. I am sorry about the anvil.

HILDE: What about the anvil?

ARVID: It is in the river now.

HILDE: (long pause) No one has ever ruined my forge for me before.

ARVID: Is that... good?

HILDE: Yes.

^(They embrace. The goat eats the ring. OLD MARTA appears from behind a barrel.)

MARTA: I'll fetch the priest. And a new anvil. And possibly a new goat.

^CURTAIN

#A Note from the Author

This play was first performed at a roadside inn to an audience of nine, one of whom was a real goat that wandered in during the second scene and refused to leave. Its performance was widely praised. The goat's, I mean.
